Matching specific utensils to cooking methods

Types of stoves (Gas stove, chulha, solar cooker)
Safety awareness regarding fire and heat

concepts.title: Sources of Food: Plants and Animals
concepts.description: Categorizing food items based on their origin, distinguishing between plant products and animal products.
key_ideas: Plant sources (grains, pulses, vegetables, fruits)
Animal sources (milk, eggs, meat, honey)
Edible parts of plants (roots, stems, leaves, flowers)

concepts.title: Food for Different Ages
concepts.description: Understanding how dietary needs and the ability to eat certain foods change from infancy to old age.
key_ideas: Liquid and soft diets for infants and the elderly
Hard foods (corn, nuts) for young and healthy people
Relationship between teeth/digestion and food choices

concepts.title: Why We Need Shelter
concepts.description: Understanding the fundamental reasons humans and animals seek shelter, focusing on protection from environmental elements and safety.
key_ideas: Protection from harsh weather like rain, heat, and cold
Safety from wild animals and thieves
Providing a place to rest and sleep securely

concepts.title: Houses and Climate
concepts.description: Analyzing how different weather conditions in various regions influence the structure and design of houses.
key_ideas: Stilt houses in areas with heavy rainfall (e.g., Assam)
Sloping roofs in snowy or rainy areas (e.g., Manali, Kashmir)
Thick mud walls in hot deserts to keep cool (e.g., Rajasthan)
Igloos made of ice in polar regions

concepts.title: Animal Shelters
concepts.description: Identifying the different types of homes animals live in, distinguishing between natural habitats and man-made shelters for domestic animals.
key_ideas: Natural homes: Nests (birds), Dens (lions), Burrows (rabbits)
Man-made homes: Sheds (cows), Stables (horses), Kennels (dogs)
Animals that carry their homes (Snails, Tortoises)

concepts.title: A Clean and Healthy House
concepts.description: Learning the essential features that make a house healthy to live in, focusing on hygiene, ventilation, and waste management.
key_ideas: Importance of sunlight and fresh air (ventilation)
Proper disposal of garbage and waste
Keeping the house free from pests and insects (wire netting)
Regular cleaning and dusting

concepts.title: Decorating Our Homes
concepts.description: Exploring how people beautify their homes using local materials and traditional art forms during festivals and daily life.
key_ideas: Using Rangoli or Kolam on floors
Decorating walls with paintings or pictures
Using flowers, leaves, and lights for festivals
Cultural significance of home decoration

concepts.description: Maps and Directions — part of the chapter on Travel.

Real-world applications of maps and directions

concepts.title: Animals Used for Transport
concepts.description: Exploration of how different animals are used to carry people and goods in various terrains, such as camels in deserts and ponies in hilly areas.
key_ideas: Camels are used in deserts.
Bullock carts are common in villages.
Ponies and mules help in hilly regions.
Elephants were used for travel in the past.

concepts.title: Special Purpose Vehicles
concepts.description: Identification of vehicles designed for specific tasks rather than just passenger travel, including emergency services and utility vehicles.
key_ideas: Ambulances carry sick people to hospitals.
Fire engines are used to put out fires.
Tractors are used for farming.
Postal vans carry letters and parcels.

concepts.title: Road Safety and Traffic Rules
concepts.description: Understanding basic safety rules to follow while walking or driving on the road to prevent accidents.
key_ideas: Traffic light colors: Red (Stop), Yellow (Wait), Green (Go).
Always use the Zebra crossing to cross the road.
Look right, then left, then right again before crossing.
Do not play on or near the road.

concepts.title: Railways and Stations
concepts.description: An introduction to train travel, the environment of a railway station, and the people who work there.
key_ideas: Trains run on tracks (rails).
Porters (coolies) help carry luggage at stations.
Trains are good for long-distance travel.
Stations have ticket counters and waiting rooms.

concepts.title: Tickets and Travel Documents
concepts.description: Understanding the requirement of purchasing tickets for public transport and the role of ticket checkers.
key_ideas: We must buy tickets for buses and trains.
A Ticket Collector (TC/TTE) checks tickets on the train.
Tickets show the destination and the price (fare).
Traveling without a ticket is against the rules.

concepts.title: Natural and Man-Made Materials

key_ideas: Core principles of natural and man-made materials
Step-by-step problem solving for natural and man-made materials
Real-world applications of natural and man-made materials

concepts.title: Indian Crafts and Artisans
concepts.description: Indian Crafts and Artisans — part of the chapter on Things We Make and Do.
key_ideas: Core principles of indian crafts and artisans
Step-by-step problem solving for indian crafts and artisans
Real-world applications of indian crafts and artisans

concepts.title: Making Pots from Clay
concepts.description: Exploration of how clay is collected, prepared, and shaped into pots using hands or a wheel, followed by the drying and baking process.
key_ideas: Clay is a natural material used to make pots and toys.
Kneading clay makes it soft and ready for shaping.
Pots are baked in a fire (kiln) to make them strong and durable.

concepts.title: Weaving and Stitching
concepts.description: An introduction to how clothes are made, focusing on the transformation of thread into fabric through weaving and fabric into clothes through stitching.
key_ideas: Weaving involves crossing two sets of threads to make cloth.
Looms are machines used for weaving fabric.
Tailors use needles, thread, and sewing machines to stitch clothes.

concepts.title: Tools of the Trade
concepts.description: Identification and analysis of specific tools used by different artisans and workers to create various objects.
key_ideas: Different professions require specific tools (e.g., potter's wheel, trowel, saw).
Tools help humans do work faster and more precisely.
Safety is important when using sharp or heavy tools.

concepts.title: Best Out of Waste
concepts.description: Learning how to reuse old or discarded materials to create useful new items or decorative art.
key_ideas: Recycling helps keep our environment clean.
Old newspapers, bottles, and boxes can be turned into crafts.
Creativity allows us to see value in things we usually throw away.
